big_case_rationale: A Bivens case with the Solicitor General and nineteen States as amici and divided argument; the judgment will govern damages suits by every federal prisoner over medical care and may confine Carlson v. Green to its facts, though an outright overruling of Bivens is unlikely and the doctrine is already narrow.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will hold that Watanabe's claim arises in a new Bivens context distinct from Carlson v. Green because the Bureau of Prisons' Administrative Remedy Program and Congress's post-Carlson prisoner-litigation legislation (the PLRA) are alternative remedial structures and special factors that Carlson never considered, applying Ziglar v. Abbasi's rule that unconsidered special factors make a context new and Egbert v. Boule's rule that any such factor forecloses the remedy at step two. It will reject respondent's argument that the Westfall Act and the PLRA ratified Carlson, will leave Carlson formally intact rather than overrule it, and will decline petitioner's invitation to overrule Bivens.

The ground will be categorical rather than fact-bound: because it rests on the Administrative Remedy Program and the PLRA, which apply to every federal prisoner, the majority's rule will mean that Eighth Amendment deliberate-indifference medical claims by federal prisoners generally present a new context and cannot proceed under Carlson, effectively confining Carlson to its own facts, rather than a narrow holding that turns on the lesser severity or non-fatal character of Watanabe's injury.
